# Our research

We follow disease along the motor unit, from the motor neuron through the junction to the muscle fibre, and bring what we learn back to the clinic.
:::

::: nm-topic
::: {}
[01]{.nm-num}

## The motor neuron

[TDP-43 loss and cryptic splicing]{.nm-line}
:::

::: {}
In most people with ALS and many with frontotemporal dementia, the RNA-binding protein TDP-43 leaves the nucleus of affected neurons. Without it, neurons splice cryptic exons into their mRNAs, which can switch off genes they need, such as UNC13A and STMN2.

We map these events in patient tissue and large RNA-seq datasets, ask which of them can be measured as biomarkers, and work with collaborators on splice-switching therapies that restore normal splicing.

[Selected papers]{.nm-kicker}

- [TDP-43 loss and ALS-risk SNPs drive mis-splicing and depletion of UNC13A.](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04436-3) *Nature*, 2022
- [TDP-43 loss induces cryptic polyadenylation in ALS/FTD.](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41593-025-02050-w) *Nature Neuroscience*, 2025
- [U7 small nuclear RNA splice-switching therapeutics for STMN2 and UNC13A in ALS.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12697360/) *bioRxiv*, 2025
:::
:::

::: {}
[02]{.nm-num}

## The junction

[Synapses and the immune response]{.nm-line}
:::

::: {}
Loss of TDP-43 disrupts synaptic function, and restoring UNC13A splicing with antisense oligonucleotides can rescue it. We are extending this work to the neuromuscular junction, where the motor neuron meets the muscle.

Cryptic exons also make new peptides. With collaborators we showed that some of them are recognised by clonally expanded CD8 T cells in ALS and inclusion body myositis, linking adaptive immunity directly to TDP-43 pathology.

[Selected papers]{.nm-kicker}

- [Loss of TDP-43 induces synaptic dysfunction that is rescued by UNC13A splice-switching ASOs.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11230273/) *bioRxiv*, 2024
- [TDP-43 pathology induces CD8+ T cell activation through cryptic epitope recognition.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12262510/) *bioRxiv*, 2025
- [Mis-spliced transcripts generate de novo proteins in TDP-43–related ALS/FTD.](https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/scitranslmed.adg7162) *Science Translational Medicine*, 2024
:::
:::

[03]{.nm-num}

## The muscle fibre

[SBMA, repeat expansions and muscle biomarkers]{.nm-line}
:::

::: {}
Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA) is caused by a CAG repeat expansion in the androgen receptor gene. Our population genetics work shows that this expansion is more common than once thought.

We follow a large SBMA cohort over time, validate outcome measures and define what counts as a meaningful change for patients, so that clinical trials are easier to interpret. In ALS, we study phosphorylated tau in skeletal muscle and develop ELISA assays for new biomarkers.

[Selected papers]{.nm-kicker}

- [Unexpected frequency of the pathogenic AR CAG repeat expansion in the general population.](https://academic.oup.com/brain/article-abstract/146/7/2723/7043521) *Brain*, 2023
- [Estimating the minimal clinically important difference of functional outcomes in SBMA.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00415-026-14032-4) *Journal of Neurology*, 2026
- [Reliability and construct validity of the Italian version of the AMAT scale in SBMA.](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10072-026-09052-x) *Neurological Sciences*, 2026
:::
